name: Mpourloto
description: Mpourloto (also spelled Bourloto) is a Greek trick-taking game closely related to French Belote. It is played by four players in partnerships using a 32-card deck. The game features bidding for trumps, declaring melds for bonus points, and a unique scoring system where the trump makers must outscore their opponents or lose all points to them ('mesa').

content.text: Mpourloto (also spelled Bourloto) is a Greek trick-taking game closely related to French Belote. It is played by four players in partnerships using a 32-card deck. The game features bidding for trumps, declaring melds for bonus points, and a unique scoring system where the trump makers must outscore their opponents or lose all points to them ('mesa').
Mpourloto is derived from French Belote, which spread throughout Europe in the 20th century. The Greek variant developed its own scoring and meld rules, distinguishing it from the French original.
4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
32-card pack (7 through Ace in each suit: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades).
5 cards to each player, one at a time. The next card is turned face up to propose trumps. After bidding, 3 more cards are dealt to each player.
